subject: Bespoke benchmarking setup and scoring criteria — ClearWell Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Theo Ramos <theo@clearwell.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearwell.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed eval plan and model recs (next steps)

Hi Theo — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a customer-specific eval on Redwood. Great context: ClearWell will be evaluating automated triage + short-form clinical summarization for outpatient encounters (~3k–6k tokens per record, mix of structured and free-text). PHI is in scope, so you called out interest in Private deployment options.

Summary of recommendations discussed:
- Recommended model family: opt for a tuned open-family baseline (Llama2/Orca style) plus a higher-capacity variant for edge cases. Tentative picks: redwood-llama2-13b-8k-quant (cost-efficient baseline) and redwood-llama2-70b-16k-q4f (higher quality for complex summaries).
- Evaluation focus: accuracy of extracted diagnosis codes (structured extraction), concise clinical summaries (length target 50–120 words), and hallucination/regression checks against a trusted reference set.
- Scoring proposal (high level): exact-match for coded fields, ROUGE-L + BERTScore for summaries, and a human spot-check for hallucination risk on the top 200 outputs.

What I attached: redwood_eval_template.md (runbook + required dataset format) and a small sample prompt set (clearwell_sample_prompts.json) so you can see the canonical prompt/metadata fields we expect.

Next steps I propose (action items):
1) You share a 500–1,000 row test export in the format in the attached template (CSV ok). Please strip any direct identifiers if you need, but flag PHI retention requirements explicitly.
2) I’ll loop in engineering (Marcus & Priyom) to confirm Hosted vs Private baseline and to provide an initial scoring rubric we can iterate on.
3) We’ll run a smoke eval (1–2 model variants) and share preliminary metrics + example failures within 3 business days of dataset receipt.

Questions for you:
- Do you have an internal threshold for acceptable hallucination rate (e.g., <2% on spot-checks)?
- Are there any output constraints we should encode in the prompt (redaction rules, required fields)?

Thanks — I’ll hold off on provisioning anything until we have your sample export.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.md (MD), clearwell_sample_prompts.json (JSON)
From: Theo Ramos <theo@clearwell.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed eval plan and model recs (next steps)

Thanks Olga — that recap is perfect. I attached a 750-row anonymized extract using the CSV layout from your template (file: clearwell_test_set.csv). The file includes: encounter_id, note_text, chief_complaint, problem_list (ICD ref), and gold_summary (our clinician-provided reference).

A few clarifications from our side:
- PHI handling: this extract is de-identified per our legal team, but the production pipeline will include limited identifiers. We need to understand tradeoffs between Hosted vs Private — compliance team will likely request Private for production but we are fine with a hosted smoke run for evaluation if you can guarantee no persistence of raw notes.
- Hallucination threshold: we don’t have a hard number — open to your recommendation. For procurement we’ll likely push for <1.5% hallucination on spot-checked cases, but we can be pragmatic for the initial run.
- Timeline: can you run the smoke eval and share a first-pass report by EOD Tuesday (3 business days)?

Attached: clearwell_test_set.csv

—Theo
Theo Ramos
Head of ML Product, ClearWell Health
theo@clearwell.ai | +1 (212) 555-0110
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: ClearWell test set + ask: scoring rubric and deployment path

Marcus / Priyom — forwarding the sample dataset from ClearWell (attached). Request: please confirm the recommended evaluation plan and whether we should run the initial smoke on Hosted (fastest) or advise Private (compliance). Key constraints:
- Dataset: 750 rows, CSV with gold_summary column.
- Goals: structured extraction (problem_list), summarization quality, hallucination risk.
- Quick deliverable: run 2 variants (13b quant baseline, 70b high-cap) and provide metrics + top-50 failure examples within 3 business days.

Please include in your reply:
- Exact scoring rubric (metrics per task and thresholds)
- Required dataset transformations / column expectations (soft failures we can handle)
- Infra recommendation for smoke run (Hosted vs Private) and any provisioning ETA
- Any red flags on the CSV (I glanced quickly — there are a few long notes >6k tokens)

I attached the standard runbook (redwood_eval_template.md) for reference.

Thanks — Olga
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: ClearWell test set + ask: scoring rubric and deployment path

Thanks for the forward, Olga. I reviewed the CSV and sketched a pragmatic plan below. We can definitely hit the 3-business-day promise for the smoke eval if ClearWell’s test set is clean enough.

Proposed scoring rubric (task-level):
1) Structured extraction (problem_list -> ICD set):
   - Metric: token-level normalized exact match and set-level recall/precision (report both).
   - Primary score: F1 (set-level) with a >0.88 target for initial pass.
2) Summarization (gold_summary):
   - Metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore (precision and recall), and a brevity penalty (measure length ratio to gold).
   - Primary score: composite (0.5*BERTScore + 0.5*ROUGE-L) with an initial target >= 0.62.
3) Hallucination / factuality:
   - Metric: human spot-check (50–200 samples) flagged as hallucinated or not, combined with an automatic Named Entity Overlap check to surface obvious hallucinations.
   - Threshold: aim for <2% hallucination on spot-checks for smoke run; production target <1.5%.

Dataset expectations / transformations:
- Required columns: encounter_id, note_text, gold_summary, problem_list (pipe-delimited ICDs).
- We will truncate notes at 6k tokens and mark rows as "long_note" for downstream analysis.
- We will seed a prefix prompt with length & redaction instructions (see attached eval_template).

Infra recommendation:
- Run smoke on Hosted first to iterate quickly (no persistence of raw notes; ephemeral cache only). For production, due to PHI concerns, advise Private deployment with KMS integration and SOC2 controls. I’ll include a short memo for the security team to speed approval.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Step 0: Validate CSV schema (PRIYOM) — 4h work to convert edge columns and flag long notes.
- Step 1: Provision two model variants in a temporary experiment (MARCUS) — couple hours if hosted GPU capacity available.
- Step 2: Run batched inference with KV caching and prefix prompts (MARCUS) — 6–8 hours for 750 rows depending on concurrency.
- Step 3: Score outputs and generate top-50 failure examples + hallucination candidates (MARCUS + PRIYOM) — deliverable artifact: metrics.csv + failures.zip.

Deliverables & ETA:
- Validation + schema fixes: end of day Monday (Priyom).
- Hosted smoke run + initial metrics + failures: Wednesday EOD (3 business days).
- Short memo for security/recommendation: Monday EOD (Marcus).

I attached the exact scoring config we’ll run (I included parameter names from the eval harness in the drive link).

Action items:
- Priyom: confirm CSV schema transforms and share estimated effort.
- Olga: confirm customer is OK with a Hosted smoke run for the initial 750-row test.

I’ll start the experiment once schema validation is complete.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
